relationships.description: Apollo Hospitals supports the operation and management of the 100-bed Duchess International Hospital in Ikeja, Lagos, to strengthen efficiency and clinical quality. The arrangement was announced when the hospital launched in October 2021.
relationships.evidence: ThisDay (11 November 2021) and New Telegraph report that operation and management of the Duchess are supported by Apollo Hospitals, India. No dated confirmation from October 2024 onward was found; the hospital's 2024 and 2025 award releases do not mention Apollo.

relationships.indian_partner: State House Clinic
relationships.description: Apollo doctors visit the State House Clinic to give free consultations and lectures, and clinic staff have been sent to Apollo in India for up to six weeks of training at no charge.
relationships.evidence: Blueprint, 29 July 2022, quotes the clinic's medical director describing a collaboration of almost six to seven years and a visiting Apollo team in Abuja. Start year is approximate, back-calculated from that quote. No later dated activity was found; a March 2024 ThisDay report records only Apollo's stated intent to partner with Nigerian hospitals.

relationships.indian_partner: Kasi Healthcare
relationships.description: Memorial specialists provide second opinions and specialist screenings, with monthly visiting specialists and training courses for Nigerian providers at Kasi's Lagos airport clinic, linked to referral of patients to Turkey. Close to a patient-referral arrangement.
relationships.evidence: BusinessDay, 27 September 2024, reports the partnership announced with Memorial's country executive. No later dated activity was found.

relationships.indian_partner: University of Abuja Teaching Hospital
relationships.description: A China-Nigeria government letter of intent names these two hospitals as the pioneer project for hospital cooperation under the 2021 FOCAC health programmes, covering knowledge sharing and research.
relationships.evidence: Within Nigeria and the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital website report the letter of intent signed in Abuja by the Chinese Ambassador and Nigeria's Health Minister in August 2022. No follow-up activity was found. The Chinese hospital's name varies between sources and is inferred.
